subject.title: Control UI fails to load on Firefox desktop behind reverse proxy — CSP blocks Vite runtime eval(), 'Control UI did not start', WebSocket 1006

question: Should maintainers keep this issue separate for Firefox reverse-proxy WebSocket proof while fixing the CSP overlap with a no-eval/Zod-jitless path, or consolidate/relax the CSP direction another way?
rationale: The source-backed CSP problem is real and overlaps an open issue, but the reported WebSocket 1006 symptom may need live proxy/browser proof before a gateway behavior change is safe; accepting unsafe-eval is a security posture decision.

options.title: Keep Strict CSP And Prove Proxy Path
options.body: Keep this issue open for Firefox reverse-proxy proof and pursue a no-eval or Zod-jitless fix for the overlapping CSP problem.

options.title: Consolidate Under CSP Thread
options.body: Fold this issue into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78362 if maintainers decide the WebSocket failure is only startup fallout from the CSP/Zod violation.

options.title: Accept CSP Relaxation
options.body: Allow unsafe-eval or another CSP relaxation only if maintainers explicitly accept the authenticated Control UI security downgrade.

recommendation.title: Keep Strict CSP And Prove Proxy Path
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for Firefox reverse-proxy proof and pursue a no-eval or Zod-jitless fix for the overlapping CSP problem.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across Control UI CSP, bootstrap contract, and WebSocket-origin hardening.
